text: Which RNA-seq aligner is described as "splice-aware," builds a splice junction database in a two-pass mode, and requires substantial RAM (~30 Gb for human)?
explanation: STAR is the splice-aware aligner that builds a junction database in its first pass and re-aligns using discovered junctions in its second pass, at the cost of high RAM usage (~30 Gb for a human genome). BWA-MEM2 and Bowtie2 are standard for genomic DNA and ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq respectively but are not splice-aware, and minimap2 is designed for long-read mapping rather than short-read RNA-seq splice alignment.
